title: $\nu_X^*$ identifies the localizing closures
statement:
Work in the standing setting of finite-type schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$ be a prime and $A$ a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$ (a finite admissible ring). For a scheme $X$ in this setting, use the unbounded derived categories of ordinary module sheaves over the constant discrete ring $A$ on the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and the comparison morphism $
u_X$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The finite-discrete coefficient identifications [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] identify this constant ring sheaf with the pulled-back condensed ring used in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and [sk-def-localizing-closure]; their module categories are transported along this ring isomorphism. On either site, $\Dctf$ means the full subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: some interval $[a,b]$ contains the cohomology of $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$ for every module sheaf $N$ in degree zero [sk-def-sfb-constructible, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. On either derived category, $\Loc(\mathcal S)$ means the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory containing $\mathcal S$ and closed under arbitrary small coproducts, with ambient coproducts (the convention [sk-def-localizing-closure]).

Then $
u_X^*$ restricts to an exact equivalence
$\Loc(\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$
preserving arbitrary small sums. For every finite-type morphism $g:X	o Y$ of standing schemes, the canonical comparisons with $g^*$ and $Rg_*$ are isomorphisms on complexes in these closures whenever evaluated in the ambient derived categories. For an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the comparison $
u_X^*j^{\mathrm{ét}}_!\simeq j^{\mathrm{proét}}_!
u_U^*$ is an isomorphism there as well. Consequently, for every chosen compactification $f=p\circ j$ in the standing setting, with $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], the composite definition $Rf_!:=Rp_*j_!$ is compatible with comparison: $
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{ét},!}\simeq Rf_{\mathrm{proét},!}
u_X^*$. This is a comparison in the ambient categories; no separate stability theorem for the operations is asserted here.

proof.text: First identify the coefficient conventions. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] the continuous-function condensed ring of finite discrete $A$ is its sheafified constant ring on profinite sets. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] its pullback to $X$ is the constant $A$-ring sheaf. Transporting module actions along this ring isomorphism leaves the underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged; its inverse transports along the inverse ring isomorphism. These exact inverse functors apply termwise to complexes and identify ambient sums, tensor products, finite Tor amplitude and the finite constant local models in the constructibility definition. Thus the ordinary coefficient categories specified here realize the finite-$A$ categories in the cited constructibility and closure nodes. By [lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison], $\nu_X^*$ is exact, fully faithful and preserves arbitrary sums on the unbounded derived categories. By [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian], specialized to the finite Noetherian coefficient ring $A$, it restricts to an equivalence $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)\simeq\Dctf(X,A)$. Thus the finite-Tor generators correspond under $\nu_X^*$.

Write $L_{\mathrm{ét}}=\Loc(\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A))$ and $L_{\mathrm{proét}}=\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$. The full replete inverse image of $L_{\mathrm{proét}}$ under $\nu_X^*$ is triangulated and closed under sums by [lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison]: shifts and distinguished triangles are preserved, and the image of a sum is the sum of its images. It contains every étale finite-Tor generator by Step 1. By the defining intersection property of $L_{\mathrm{ét}}$, it contains $L_{\mathrm{ét}}$. Thus $\nu_X^*(L_{\mathrm{ét}})\subseteq L_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The target closure and its ambient sums use [sk-def-localizing-closure]; the same intersection definition on the étale side was specified in the statement.

Let $\mathcal I$ be the full replete essential image of $L_{\mathrm{ét}}$. For $M_i\cong
u_X^*K_i$ with $K_i\in L_{\mathrm{ét}}$, the ambient coproduct satisfies $ igoplus_i M_i\cong
u_X^*( igoplus_i K_i)$ by [lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison], and $ igoplus_i K_i\in L_{\mathrm{ét}}$. Likewise $M[n]\cong
u_X^*(K[n])$ for every integer $n$; the empty coproduct gives the zero object. For a map $
u_X^*K	o
u_X^*K'$ with $K,K'\in L_{\mathrm{ét}}$, fullness lifts the map to $u:K	o K'$. Complete $u$ to a distinguished triangle with third object $C\in L_{\mathrm{ét}}$; exactness sends it to a distinguished triangle with the prescribed first arrow. Its third object is isomorphic to any cone of that arrow, so $\mathcal I$ is triangulated. It contains $\Dctf(X,A)$ by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. The smallest-localizing-subcategory property of [sk-def-localizing-closure] therefore gives $L_{\mathrm{proét}}\subseteq\mathcal I$. Step 2 gives the reverse inclusion. Full faithfulness restricts to full subcategories, so this is an equivalence; its exactness and sum preservation are those of $
u_X^*$, since both closures have the ambient triangles and sums.

For any $g:X	o Y$, [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] states the inverse-image comparison $g_{\mathrm{proét}}^*
u_Y^*\simeq
u_X^*g_{\mathrm{ét}}^*$ on the unbounded derived categories, compatible with composition. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] supplies the natural sheaf comparison $
u_X^*j^{\mathrm{ét}}_!\simeq j^{\mathrm{proét}}_!
u_U^*$, compatible with open composition. Both $j_!$ are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], and $
u^*$ is exact by [lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison]. Thus applying the comparison degreewise yields an isomorphism of complexes compatible with differentials; naturality makes it commute with chain maps, and exactness lets it descend through quasi-isomorphisms. The result holds for unbounded complexes. For finite-type $g$, [lem-sfb-unbounded-direct-image-comparison] supplies the canonical unbounded direct-image isomorphism. Restricting these ambient comparisons to the closures gives the asserted compatibilities.

For a fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, compose the two isomorphisms of Step 4:
$
u_Y^*Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}j^{\mathrm{ét}}_!K\xrightarrow{\alpha_{p,j_!K}}Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}
u_{\overline X}^*j^{\mathrm{ét}}_!K\xrightarrow{Rp_*(e_{j,K})}Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}j^{\mathrm{proét}}_!
u_X^*K$.
The first is an isomorphism for every unbounded input and the second is the image of an isomorphism under a functor. Their composite is natural in $K$ and is precisely the comparison for the stipulated composite definition $Rf_!=Rp_*j_!$. This proves the last clause without assuming any stability property of $Rg_*$ on the closures.
